annotation.kind: exact matrix form of Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.6)-(4.12)

assumptions: The matrices and vectors are the real specialization of the quantities in Theorem 4.1.
a is p_(j+1)^T Q_j, b is P_j^T q_(j+1), and p55LastBasis k is e_j.
ha and hb are the last-coordinate consequences of local biorthogonality used for the two rank-one support claims.
hmaster is equation (4.10), with F and G denoting the two projected error terms.
hDelta and herror are the decompositions defining K-L and N-M in Theorem 4.1.
hCT and hDT are the strict-triangular commutator observations made immediately after equation (4.10).
The denominator assumptions make the two quotient statements explicit over Lean's totalized real division.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p55_t3_loss_of_biorthogonality (k : Nat) (T C Delta D F G K L N M : P55Matrix (k + 1)) (a b z w : P55Vector (k + 1)) (beta gamma theta : Real) (ha : a (Fin.last k) = 0) (hb : b (Fin.last k) = 0) (hmaster : gamma • p55Outer (p55LastBasis k) a - beta • p55Outer b (p55LastBasis k) = (C * T - T * C) + (Delta * T - T * Delta) + (D * T - T * D) + (F - G)) (hDelta : Delta * T - T * Delta = K - L) (herror : F - G = N - M) (hCT : p55StrictLower (C * T - T * C)) (hDT : p55StrictUpper (D * T - T * D)) (hK : p55StrictLower K) (hL : p55StrictUpper L) (hN : p55StrictLower N) (hM : p55StrictUpper M) (hz : T *ᵥ z = theta • z) (hw : w ᵥ* T = theta • w) (hgamma : gamma * (w ⬝ᵥ p55LastBasis k) != 0) (hbeta : beta * (p55LastBasis k ⬝ᵥ z) != 0) : a ⬝ᵥ z = (w ⬝ᵥ ((K + N) *ᵥ z)) / (gamma * (w ⬝ᵥ p55LastBasis k)) and w ⬝ᵥ b = (w ⬝ᵥ ((L + M) *ᵥ z)) / (beta * (p55LastBasis k ⬝ᵥ z))
formal_statement.plain_language: Derive both loss-of-biorthogonality formulas by splitting equation (4.10) into its strict lower and upper parts and cancelling the two commutators against a left and right eigenvector.

informal_proof: Equation (4.10) is a sum of a strictly lower and a strictly upper matrix on each side. Uniqueness of that decomposition yields (4.11) and (4.12). Apply w_i^H on the left and z_i on the right. The left and right eigenvector equations make each commutator scalar vanish, leaving the two numerators. The two nonzero scalar factors can then be divided out.
informal_statement: Prove the two exact loss-of-biorthogonality identities in Theorem 4.1.

tier_rationale: The task requires proving the support of two boundary rank-one matrices, constructing and using uniqueness of a strict-lower/strict-upper decomposition, reorganizing the full projected recurrence, cancelling two noncommutative matrix commutators with left and right eigenvector equations, and deriving two quotient identities. The exact N proof has 170 physical lines and is at least as demanding as the lower end of validated T2/T3 workloads rather than a short Mathlib import exercise. The exact L mathematical proof is byte-identical and uses no NumStability declaration, establishing that the frozen library provides no speedup.
